leftEvidence.title: The LORD asks how long Israel will refuse belief

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: The LORD asks Moses how long the people will despise him and refuse to believe despite signs among them.
points.right: Hebrews quotes the psalm’s “today,” warns against an unbelieving heart, and asks who rebelled after hearing.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: He proposes plague, dispossession, and a new nation from Moses greater than Israel.
points.right: Those who sinned fell in the wilderness, and the conclusion names unbelief as the reason they could not enter.

payload.posture: Numbers asks how long Israel will refuse belief after signs; Hebrews concludes that unbelief prevented entry.

rightEvidence.role: Refusal remembered as unbelief and lost rest
rightEvidence.title: Hebrews asks who rebelled and why they could not enter

payload.tension: Hebrews applies the event to new hearers while Numbers preserves the crisis inside its own narrative sequence.
payload.title: Refusal named as unbelief
